question: What type of trees are found in mountain forests in India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (05/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: Ash
Chir
Maple
Cactus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chir

Explanation:
Mountain forests in India are primarily found in the Himalayan region. These forests vary with altitude. Chir (Pine) trees grow at medium to high altitudes (1000-2200 meters) and are considered the main trees of the temperate zone. Chir wood is soft and used for furniture, construction, and resin production. While Ash and Maple are mainly found in temperate forests of the northern hemisphere, Chir is more common in Indian mountain forests. Cactus is a desert plant. Therefore, among the given options, Chir is correct.

☛ What is the scientific name of Chir? → Pinus roxburghii
☛ What type of wood is Chir? → Softwood
☛ What is the sticky substance obtained from Chir called? → Resin
☛ Which is the main Chir tree in the Himalayan region? → Chir Pine (Pinus roxburghii)
question_hi: भारत के पर्वतीय वनों में किस प्रकार के पेड़ पाए जाते हैं? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (05/04/2021) Shift 1)
options_hi: ऐश
चीड़
मेपल
कैक्टस
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है चीड़

Explanation:
भारत के पर्वतीय वन मुख्यतः हिमालय क्षेत्र में पाए जाते हैं। ये वन ऊँचाई के अनुसार बदलते हैं। चीड़ (Pine) के पेड़ मध्यम से अधिक ऊँचाई (1000-2200 मीटर) पर उगते हैं और इन्हें शीतोष्ण क्षेत्र का प्रमुख वृक्ष माना जाता है। चीड़ की लकड़ी मुलायम होती है और इसका उपयोग फर्नीचर, निर्माण और रेज़िन उत्पादन में होता है। जबकि ऐश और मेपल प्रमुखतः उत्तरी गोलार्ध के शीतोष्ण वनों में पाए जाते हैं, भारत के पर्वतीय वनों में चीड़ अधिक सामान्य है। कैक्टस शुष्क क्षेत्रों का पौधा है। इसलिए दिए गए विकल्पों में चीड़ सही है।

☛ हिमालयी क्षेत्र का प्रमुख चीड़ वृक्ष कौन सा है? → Chir Pine (Pinus roxburghii)

question: In which state can one find the Himalayan Yew? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (05/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: Arunachal Pradesh
Uttarakhand
Sikkim
Jammu & Kashmir
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Arunachal Pradesh

Explanation:
The Himalayan Yew (Taxus wallichiana) is a medicinal plant found in the Himalayan region. It is primarily distributed in states like Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, and Jammu & Kashmir. However, Arunachal Pradesh has the highest diversity and density of this species. The compound taxol derived from this plant is used in cancer treatment. The Himalayan Yew is classified as Endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).

☛ Anti-cancer compound from Himalayan Yew → Taxol
☛ IUCN status of Himalayan Yew → Endangered

☛ Main distribution area of Himalayan Yew → Eastern Himalayas, especially Arunachal Pradesh

Explanation:
हिमालयन यू (Taxus wallichiana) एक औषधीय पादप है जो हिमालयी क्षेत्र में पाया जाता है। यह मुख्य रूप से अरुणाचल प्रदेश, हिमाचल प्रदेश, उत्तराखंड, सिक्किम और जम्मू-कश्मीर में पाया जाता है, लेकिन अरुणाचल प्रदेश में इसकी सबसे अधिक विविधता और घनत्व पाया जाता है। इस पौधे से प्राप्त टैक्सोल नामक यौगिक कैंसर के उपचार में उपयोग होता है। हिमालयन यू को अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रकृति संरक्षण संघ (IUCN) द्वारा संकटग्रस्त प्रजाति के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया गया है।

question: Which is the only Indian state to share its boundary with the state of Sikkim? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (05/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: Assam
West Bengal
Mizoram
Odisha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is West Bengal

Explanation:
Sikkim is a northeastern state of India, which joined the Indian Union in 1975. It is bordered by three international boundaries - China, Bhutan, and Nepal. Within India, Sikkim shares its boundary only with the state of West Bengal. The Darjeeling district of West Bengal touches the southern boundary of Sikkim. Sikkim has an area of about 7,096 sq km and is the second smallest state in India. Its capital is Gangtok. It is known for its biodiversity and tourism. In 2018, it became India's first organic state.

question: The Murlen National Park is located in which state? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (05/04/2021) Shift 1)

question: Name the river on which the Indira Sagar Dam is built. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (05/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: Yamuna
Kaveri
Ganges
Narmada
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Narmada

Explanation:
Indira Sagar Dam is a multipurpose project located on the Narmada River in Madhya Pradesh. It is the largest dam under the Narmada Valley Development Project. The dam is 92 meters high and 653 meters long. It generates 1000 MW of hydroelectricity and provides irrigation. The dam is situated in the Khandwa district of Madhya Pradesh. The Narmada River flows through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat. The project was approved in 1984 and completed in 2003. The reservoir created by the dam is called Indira Sagar, which is the second largest man-made reservoir in India.

question: _______ is the closest star of the Earth. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (05/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: Altair
Sun
Vega
Moon
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sun

Explanation:
The closest star to Earth is the Sun, located approximately 150 million kilometers away. It is a G-type main-sequence star that provides light and energy essential for life on Earth. question: Which of the following is used as a fuel in nuclear reactors? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: Cobalt
Copper
Uranium
Iodine
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Uranium

Explanation:
Uranium is used as a fuel in nuclear reactors because it is a fissile material. The isotope Uranium-235 undergoes fission upon neutron absorption, releasing enormous energy used for electricity generation. Natural uranium contains only 0.7% U-235, with the rest being U-238. For reactor use, uranium is enriched to increase U-235 concentration. Cobalt, copper, and iodine are not fissile and thus cannot sustain a nuclear chain reaction, making them unsuitable as nuclear fuel.
